body.statement: Sanity Corollary (one-stage Chen reduction). Let \(H=1\), suppose \(\mathcal K(p)\ne\varnothing\), and let \(S_2\) play Chen's always-observed \(F\) role. For every \(s\) with \(p(S_1=s)>0\) and every \(a\in\mathcal A\), behavior positivity implies \(p(S_1=s,A_1=a)>0\). In each such cell define the observed respondent matrix and nonrespondent vector from the observed reward, response, and shadow table by \(A_{s,a}[s',r]=p(M_1=1,S_2=s',R_1=r\mid S_1=s,A_1=a)\) and \(\boldsymbol\beta_{s,a}[s']=p(M_1=0,S_2=s'\mid S_1=s,A_1=a)\). Suppose cellwise response positivity holds: \(\sum_{s'\in\mathcal S}A_{s,a}[s',r]>0\) for every \((s,a)\in\mathcal X_{SA}(p)\) and \(r\in\mathcal R\). Then the global fiber decomposes cellwise as \(\mathcal K(p)\cong\prod_{(s,a)\in\mathcal X_{SA}(p)}\mathcal W_{s,a}\), where \(\mathcal W_{s,a}=\{w\in\mathbb R_+^{|\mathcal R|}:A_{s,a}w=\boldsymbol\beta_{s,a}\}\), and its value image is \(\Theta_I(p)=\{\sum_{(s,a)\in\mathcal X_{SA}(p)}p(S_1=s)\pi_1(a\mid s)\theta_{s,a}:\theta_{s,a}\in\mathcal J_{s,a}\}\). Hence the endpoints are the corresponding weighted sums of the Chen cell-program endpoints. If every positive-mass cell matrix satisfies the precise full-column-rank condition \(\operatorname{rank}(A_{s,a})=|\mathcal R|\), necessarily with \(|\mathcal S|\ge|\mathcal R|\), then feasibility makes every \(\mathcal W_{s,a}\) a singleton and the one-stage value is point identified. This is the cell program of Chen, Simchi-Levi, and Xiong, arXiv:2602.16061v1, source section titled \emph{Partial Identification via Linear Programs}, equation label \(\texttt{opt:mnar-with-shadow-matrix-form-theta}\), and proposition label \(\texttt{prop:point-id-mean}\).
body.justification: The one-stage decomposition is a non-novel sanity corollary pinned to Chen, Simchi-Levi, and Xiong, arXiv:2602.16061v1, source section titled ``Partial Identification via Linear Programs,'' equation label \(\texttt{opt:mnar-with-shadow-matrix-form-theta}\), and proposition label \(\texttt{prop:point-id-mean}\).
body.gap: The cited proposition already gives the static sharp interval and full-column-rank point-identification result; the corollary only verifies that the dynamic notation reduces cell by cell under explicit response positivity.
body.consumer: Existing static weak-shadow software becomes a regression test for the dynamic implementation.
body.proof_tex:
We prove the proposed statement, which explicitly assumes \(\mathcal K(p)\neq\varnothing\).  This compatibility condition is needed because otherwise the Chen systems may be infeasible and the displayed endpoint minima and maxima are not defined.

Fix \(H=1\).  At the only decision time, \(H_1^F=H_1^O=S_1\).  Choose any \(q\in\mathcal K(p)\), which is possible by \(\mathrm{ass{:}model\text{-}compatibility}\).  Observed marginalization and \(\mathrm{ass{:}behavior\text{-}factorization}\) give, for \(p(S_1=s)>0\),
\[
 p(S_1=s,A_1=a)=q_1^O(s,a)
 =\mu_1(a\mid s)\sum_{a'}q_1^O(s,a')
 =\mu_1(a\mid s)p(S_1=s).
\]
By \(\mathrm{ass{:}behavior\text{-}positivity}\), this is at least \(\epsilon p(S_1=s)>0\).  Thus every action belongs to a positive-mass cell whenever \(p(S_1=s)>0\).

Fix such a cell \(C=(S_1=s,A_1=a)\), and for a candidate completion write
\[
 b_m(r,s')=\Pr_q(R_1=r,M_1=m,S_2=s'\mid C),\qquad m\in\{0,1\}.
\]
Observed marginalization fixes
\[
 b_1(r,s')=A_{s,a}[s',r],\qquad
 \sum_{r\in\mathcal R}b_0(r,s')=\boldsymbol\beta_{s,a}[s'].
\]
Put
\[
 \alpha_r=\sum_{u\in\mathcal S}A_{s,a}[u,r].
\]
The stated response-positivity condition says \(\alpha_r>0\) for every \(r\).  Conditionalizing the weak-shadow cross-products is legitimate because \(p(C)>0\); the common factor \(p(C)^2\) cancels.  Thus, for every \(u,s'\in\mathcal S\),
\[
 A_{s,a}[u,r]\,b_0(r,s')=b_0(r,u)\,A_{s,a}[s',r].
\]
Summing this equality over \(u\) gives
\[
 \alpha_r b_0(r,s')=A_{s,a}[s',r]\sum_{u\in\mathcal S}b_0(r,u).
\]
Division by \(\alpha_r>0\) is therefore valid.  Defining
\[
 w_r=\frac{\sum_u b_0(r,u)}{\alpha_r}\geq0
\]
yields the necessary representation
\[
 b_0(r,s')=A_{s,a}[s',r]w_r.
\]
Summing over \(r\) proves
\[
 (A_{s,a}w)[s']=\sum_r A_{s,a}[s',r]w_r
 =\sum_r b_0(r,s')=\boldsymbol\beta_{s,a}[s'],
\]
so \(w\in\mathcal W_{s,a}\).

Conversely, given any \(w\in\mathcal W_{s,a}\), set
\[
 b_1(r,s')=A_{s,a}[s',r],\qquad
 b_0(r,s')=A_{s,a}[s',r]w_r.
\]
These arrays are nonnegative, their nonrespondent shadow marginal is \(A_{s,a}w=\boldsymbol\beta_{s,a}\), and their total mass is
\[
 \sum_{r,s'}b_1(r,s')+\sum_{s'}\boldsymbol\beta_{s,a}[s']=1
\]
by the observed conditional table.  Moreover, both sides of every weak-shadow cross-product equal
\[
 A_{s,a}[u,r]A_{s,a}[s',r]w_r.
\]
Thus the construction is sufficient.  It is inverse to the preceding map.  Since, at \(H=1\), no restriction contains variables from two distinct positive-mass \((s,a)\)-cells, assembling the conditional arrays with weights
\[
 p(S_1=s,A_1=a)=p(S_1=s)\mu_1(a\mid s)
\]
gives the claimed bijection
\[
 \mathcal K(p)\cong\prod_{(s,a)\in\mathcal X_{SA}(p)}\mathcal W_{s,a}.
\]
Zero-mass states have all corresponding complete atoms equal to zero and introduce no extra coordinate.

The conditional reward mean associated with \(w\) is
\[
 \theta_{s,a}
 =\sum_{r,s'}r\{b_1(r,s')+b_0(r,s')\}
 =\mathbf 1^\top A_{s,a}\operatorname{diag}((r)_{r\in\mathcal R})(w+\mathbf 1),
\]
which is exactly an element of \(\mathcal J_{s,a}\) by \(\mathrm{def{:}static\text{-}chen\text{-}cell\text{-}program}\).  Substituting the cell factorization into \(\mathrm{def{:}stage\text{-}value}\), and using \(\mu_1(a\mid s)>0\), gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 V_\pi(q)
 &=\sum_{s,a}p(S_1=s)\mu_1(a\mid s)
   \frac{\pi_1(a\mid s)}{\mu_1(a\mid s)}\,\theta_{s,a}\\
 &=\sum_{(s,a)\in\mathcal X_{SA}(p)}p(S_1=s)\pi_1(a\mid s)\theta_{s,a}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The cell coordinates vary independently and every displayed weight is nonnegative, so minimizing or maximizing the last sum is achieved by minimizing or maximizing each \(\mathcal J_{s,a}\) separately.  This proves the asserted value image and endpoint formulas.

Finally, if \(\operatorname{rank}(A_{s,a})=|\mathcal R|\) and \(w,w'\in\mathcal W_{s,a}\), then
\[
 A_{s,a}(w-w')=0.
\]
Full column rank implies \(w=w'\).  Compatibility supplies existence, so each \(\mathcal W_{s,a}\) is a singleton.  Since
\[
 \operatorname{rank}(A_{s,a})\leq\min\{|\mathcal S|,|\mathcal R|\},
\]
full column rank necessarily requires \(|\mathcal S|\geq|\mathcal R|\).  The product fiber therefore has a unique reward-completion coordinate in every positive-mass cell, and the displayed value image is a singleton.  This proves point identification.
